notes: What is new and fixed in 0.3.0 is shown in Maieutica before you agree to update.

added: The agent now reads your files as Claude reads them: pictures and photos (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) are seen, a PDF’s pages are seen with their text — scanned pages, charts and photos included — and Excel and PowerPoint files are read as their text.
Before you choose a file, the Sources page says which kinds can be added, and the file dialog offers just those first.
A file that cannot be read is refused when you choose it, with what to do: a HEIC photo saved as JPEG, an older Word, Excel or PowerPoint file saved in the newer format, or a file over 20 MB split.
A photo is sent without where, when and with what it was taken.
The agent reads every file to its end before it reports, or says what it leaves out and why. “What was read” shows which pages of a PDF were seen.
Maieutica asks again what it may send, because files now go as they are. The page says why, and marks what is new.
0.3.0 stores your curricula in a newer way. Once it has written to them, a computer of yours still on 0.2 cannot open them until it is updated too.
fixed: Under “How is it going?” and in “How you asked to be taught”, a press while an answer was being saved did nothing. Every button there now waits, marked, until it is saved.

added: Every step now reads in Maieutica’s reading type and line length, in the app and when you open it from your folder.
A step can draw a picture where it explains faster. Each picture has a caption and says in words what it shows, and it moves only when you click its own button.

Now and then, under a step, Maieutica asks how it is going: too easy, about right or too hard, more depth or a higher level, more said or less. The agent is told with every step it writes, until you change it.
“How you asked to be taught” shows what you said, and lets you change or forget it, or stop being asked. Nothing in it is worked out from what you do.
If you say a step was too hard after the next ones were written, Maieutica offers to write those again. The earlier versions stay in your folder.
The agent plans each module’s steps, so a step says where it is: step 2 of 5.
Have a module’s planned steps written while you read, or every module’s, with one click that says how many. It stops at a limit or when you press Stop, and never goes on by itself.
A new curriculum can be given, beside its name, what you want from it, in your own words. The agent reads it before its first question. You can change it on the Questions and Goal pages.
Frequent actions now have keys, shown beside them: ← and → among steps, Ctrl+Enter to send, Esc to stop the agent, and Ctrl+K for every action on the page.
0.2.0 stores your curricula in a newer way. Once it has written to them, a computer of yours still on 0.1 cannot open them until it is updated too.

fixed: In a narrow or zoomed window, “Cannot tell if you are signed in” no longer takes half the window with its reason. Press it to read why, with “Check again” under the reason.
When Maieutica is slow to answer “Sign out”, the window now waits until it knows how the sign-out ended, instead of saying it cannot tell.
A copy of your account’s details that Maieutica could not remove when you signed out is removed again the next time it starts. If it still cannot be, Settings › Signing in says where it is.
An organisation named after the part of your email before the @, such as “richard’s Organization”, is no longer shown as its name, in the bar or in Settings.
Starting Maieutica a second time no longer spoils an update the first was about to install.
When an update is not installed, Maieutica now says what its check found, instead of always saying the file was changed on this computer.
A download that brings more than its announced size is stopped, and nothing of it is kept.
A link from Maieutica to one version on getmaieutica.com now opens that version, whatever its number.

fixedTopics.title: Signing in and paying for the agent

added: Maieutica helps you work out what you need to learn, then teaches it one step at a time. It asks you a few questions, looks into the subject, and agrees a goal with you before it writes anything.
The agent is told never to note your health, money, family, beliefs, politics, sexuality or gender, or what an employer should not read. A note that plainly says one of these about you is refused.
Your curricula are yours. They are kept on this computer, or in a folder you choose, and nothing in them is scored. Keep them on a shared or synced drive to use them from your other computers too.
If your curricula say they were written by a newer Maieutica, it names the file, changes nothing, and offers the version that reads them.
Sign in with your Claude plan from the window, without a terminal. Or have the agent paid by your own API key, kept in this computer’s password store and read only by Maieutica.
Settings shows who is signed in and on which plan, and lets you sign out or switch account.
An API key typed or pasted where the agent would read it is never sent or kept. Maieutica says why, and leaves the rest of what you typed in the box.
On Windows, Maieutica installs for you alone, with everything it needs, and keeps a log you can send when something goes wrong. On Linux it installs from a .deb.

Maieutica looks for a newer version by itself, and the check carries nothing about you. Before anything is downloaded, it shows what the new version changes. It installs only what its publisher signed, and only when you press restart and nothing would be lost.
Settings › About Maieutica shows which version you have, and which version of the agent’s program came with it.
The download page lists every version, with each file’s size and checksum.
